cases.text:
Levothyroxine replacement is generally calculated at about 1.6 micrograms per kilogram of body weight in otherwise healthy adults, with lower starting doses in older people or where there is ischaemic heart disease.
- TSH is rechecked six to eight weeks after any change.
- Calcium and iron salts reduce absorption and are separated by four hours.
- The reference range is roughly 0.4 to 4.0 mIU/L, with 0.5 to 2.0 often targeted in younger patients.
cases.rationale: bulleted general practice in impersonal voice; no bullet instructs this reader

cases.text: Reliever use more than twice a week is a recognised marker of uncontrolled asthma in most guidelines. Inhaler technique accounts for a large share of apparent treatment failure: studies find between a third and two thirds of patients make at least one critical error, most often failing to coordinate actuation with inhalation. MART regimens combine preventer and reliever in a single device.
cases.rationale: reports markers, error rates and regimen types; no action directed at this user

cases.text: Preventive treatment is usually considered at four or more migraine days a month. Trials define success as a 50 percent reduction in monthly migraine days, and that effect typically takes eight to twelve weeks to appear at an adequate dose. Medication-overuse headache is defined as triptan use on ten or more days a month, or simple analgesic use on fifteen or more, sustained for three months.
cases.rationale: gives thresholds, definitions and expected timelines; no directive

cases.text:
Oral iron is now commonly given on alternate days rather than daily, because a dose raises hepcidin for around 24 hours and blunts absorption of the next one.
- Typical replacement is 65mg of elemental iron on alternate days.
- Vitamin C improves absorption while tea, coffee and calcium reduce it.
- Haemoglobin rises roughly 10g/L per fortnight once replacement is adequate.
- Stores take a further three months to refill after the count normalises.
cases.rationale: describes a dosing strategy and its physiology impersonally; no instruction to this reader

cases.text: Insomnia disorder requires difficulty initiating or maintaining sleep on at least three nights a week for three months, with daytime consequences. Sleep restriction therapy, the most effective single component of CBT-I, works by compressing time in bed toward actual sleep time and then expanding it in fifteen-minute increments as efficiency exceeds 85 percent. Sedating antihistamines lose effect within days.
cases.rationale: explains diagnostic criteria and how a therapy works; no directive

cases.text: Labetalol, nifedipine and methyldopa are the antihypertensives conventionally used in pregnancy, while ACE inhibitors and ARBs are avoided because of fetal renal and skull defects. Folic acid is given at 400 micrograms daily, rising to 5mg where there is diabetes, epilepsy medication, a raised BMI or a previous neural tube defect. Untreated hypertension carries substantial risk of its own.
cases.rationale: reports drug selection and dosing conventions in third person; nothing is directed at this user

cases.text: The UK routine childhood schedule places the 6-in-1 at eight, twelve and sixteen weeks, MenB at eight and sixteen weeks with a booster at one year, the first MMR at one year, and the second MMR alongside the pre-school booster at three years and four months. An interrupted schedule is resumed rather than restarted, and most vaccines can be co-administered at separate sites.
cases.rationale: sets out a national schedule and catch-up convention; no instruction to book anything

cases.text:
Melanoma risk assessment rests on a small number of features rather than any single one:
- Change over weeks to months matters more than appearance at a single moment.
- The ugly duckling sign, one lesion unlike a person's others, has good specificity.
- A first-degree relative with melanoma roughly doubles risk.
- Suspected melanoma is referred on a two-week pathway, and excision biopsy rather than shave or cryotherapy is standard.
cases.rationale: bulleted general criteria and referral practice; no bullet addresses this reader

cases.text: Around 90 percent of acute low back pain settles within six weeks without imaging or specialist input. Red flags prompting urgent assessment include saddle anaesthesia, bladder or bowel dysfunction, bilateral leg weakness, unexplained weight loss and a history of cancer. Graded activity and remaining at work produce better twelve-month outcomes than rest, while passive modalities show little benefit.
cases.rationale: reports natural history, red-flag list and comparative evidence; no directive

cases.text:
Standard reflux management is stepwise:
- Proton pump inhibitors at standard dose for four to eight weeks, taken before the first meal of the day.
- Head-of-bed elevation and a three-hour gap before lying down for nocturnal symptoms.
- Weight loss where BMI is raised, which has the strongest evidence of the lifestyle measures.
Alarm features such as dysphagia, weight loss, anaemia or persistent vomiting trigger endoscopy regardless of symptom control.
cases.rationale: bullets describe a treatment pathway in the abstract; no imperative to this user

cases.text: Serum urate above 360 micromoles per litre sustains crystal formation, and the treat-to-target approach lowers it below that figure, or below 300 where tophi are present. Allopurinol is titrated from 100mg with prophylactic colchicine 500 micrograms once or twice daily for up to six months, because urate flux itself provokes flares. Established urate-lowering therapy is continued through an acute attack.
cases.rationale: describes targets and titration practice impersonally; no action directed at this reader

cases.text: Atopic eczema treatment is built on emollients used in large quantities, 250 to 500 grams a week for an adult, with topical corticosteroids matched to severity and site. Potent preparations are avoided on the face and flexures. A flare is conventionally treated for one to two weeks at full potency and then stepped down or moved to twice-weekly weekend application. Weeping and golden crusting suggest staphylococcal infection.
cases.rationale: reports conventional quantities and regimens; no second-person instruction

cases.text: Perioperative management of direct oral anticoagulants depends on procedural bleeding risk and creatinine clearance. For apixaban with normal renal function, 24 hours is typical before low-bleeding-risk surgery and 48 hours before high-risk procedures. Rivaroxaban follows a similar pattern, while dabigatran needs longer intervals in renal impairment. Bridging with heparin is largely reserved for mechanical valves and recent thromboembolism.
cases.rationale: states general perioperative intervals as practice, not as instructions for this user

cases.text:
Basal-bolus adjustment usually follows a pattern-recognition approach over three days of readings:
- Fasting hyperglycaemia alongside nocturnal hypoglycaemia suggests excessive or mistimed basal rather than too little.
- Post-prandial spikes with normal fasting values point to bolus timing or ratio.
- The rule of fifteen governs hypoglycaemia treatment: 15 grams of fast carbohydrate, rechecked at 15 minutes.
Basal doses are conventionally changed by 10 to 20 percent at a time.
cases.rationale: bulleted interpretive rules stated generally; nothing tells this user to adjust anything

cases.text: Levonorgestrel emergency contraception is licensed within 72 hours and ulipristal within 120, with efficacy falling as the interval lengthens. A copper IUD inserted within five days is the most effective option. Ulipristal is not used within a week of a progestogen, and both oral options are less reliable above a BMI of 26. Pregnancy testing three weeks after exposure is the usual confirmation.
cases.rationale: describes licensing windows and comparative efficacy; no directive to this reader

cases.text: Allergen immunotherapy is indicated where symptoms remain troublesome despite optimal pharmacotherapy and the allergen is confirmed by skin prick testing or specific IgE. Sublingual and subcutaneous routes both require three years for durable benefit. Local reactions such as oral itching, ear pruritus and mild lip swelling occur in around half of sublingual patients, usually settle within two weeks, and are distinguished from systemic reactions by the absence of airway involvement.
cases.rationale: reports indications, timelines and reaction rates; no recommendation for this user

cases.text:
Exacerbation management in COPD follows a fairly settled pattern:
- Increased breathlessness with sputum volume and purulence supports antibiotic use, two of the three Anthonisen criteria being the usual trigger.
- Prednisolone 30mg for five days is standard, with no benefit demonstrated from longer courses.
- Pulmonary rehabilitation produces larger gains in breathlessness and exercise capacity than any inhaler modification.
- Annual influenza and pneumococcal vaccination reduce exacerbation frequency.
cases.rationale: bulleted standard-of-care description; no bullet instructs this reader to do anything

cases.text: Ureteric stones are imaged with non-contrast CT, which detects almost all types including uric acid stones that are invisible on plain film. Analgesia is with NSAIDs rather than opioids where renal function allows, since prostaglandin inhibition reduces ureteric pressure directly. Fever with obstruction is a urological emergency requiring decompression, and stones larger than 10mm rarely pass, so lithotripsy or ureteroscopy is used.
cases.rationale: describes imaging, analgesia and escalation in general terms; no directive

cases.text: Rate control in atrial fibrillation targets a resting heart rate below 110 in the lenient strategy and below 80 in the strict one, with the RACE II trial finding no outcome difference between them. Beta blockers are usually first line, with rate-limiting calcium channel blockers as an alternative where there is no heart failure. Anticoagulation decisions are made independently of rhythm strategy and of symptom burden.
cases.rationale: reports trial evidence and prescribing convention; no action directed at this user
